newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-SAS seen meeting own expectations.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-SAS seen meeting own expectations.

text.p: Analysts expect Scandinavian Airlines System (SAS) to more or less match its own forecast of a fall in 1996 pre-tax profits to 1.74 billion Swedish crowns from 1995's 2.63 billion when its publishes its annual accounts on Monday.

"It would surprise me very much if SAS does not meet its own expectations, which were made public in the middle of November, halfway through the (fourth quarter) accounting period," an aviation industry analyst said.
An average of 10 analysts' forecasts predicted full-year pre-tax profits of 1.72 billion Swedish crowns.
Individual predictions ranged from 1.67 to 1.77 billion Swedish crowns.

The carrier, owned by the governments of Denmark, Norway and Sweden and private investors, has seen earnings hit by increased competition in its home market but has vowed to fight back by cutting costs, lowering fares and improving service.

Industry sources say it plans to expand its present partnership with United Airlines, Lufthansa and Thai International into a powerful global alliance to rival the proposed link-up between British Airways (BA) and American Airlines.
The sources name Brazil's Varig, Japan's All Nippon Airways O#9202q.L, South African Airways, Air Canada and British Midland as likely new partners.

SAS refuses to confirm or deny the report but appeared to hint that a deal was in the air on Thursday when it said that any expansion of the existing alliance would leave its present ownership structure unchanged.
It also said on Thursday that it had agreed to expand its passenger alliance with Lufthansa to cover freight operations. --Steve Weizman, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969650.
